groups.title: Define
groups.intro: Name a motion once, by what it does (its verb) and its keyframes, then attach it anywhere by that name.

groups.title: Attach
groups.intro: Bind a defined motion to an element: from HTML with connectMotion, or in code with motion().

groups.title: Play
groups.intro: Animate any CSS property over a token, cascade a group, and the handles, runtime and providers that play the frames.

groups.title: Values
groups.intro: A continuous value, from the pointer, the scroll, a state or the time, written to a CSS variable or counted as text.

groups.title: Gestures
groups.intro: Drag, swipe and reorder, each with a keyboard alternative.

groups.title: Sequences
groups.intro: Steps that play in order from one root, with one handle to play, pause and seek them.

groups.title: Layout
groups.intro: An element that changes its place or size travels to the new one; elements that share a key morph into each other.

groups.title: Text and SVG
groups.intro: Split text into words, characters or lines; draw a stroke, and morph one path into another.

groups.title: Scroll and pages
groups.intro: Reveal on entry, link a motion to the scroll, scroll to a target, and change pages with a direction.

groups.title: Policy and accessibility
groups.intro: Read and follow the reduced-motion policy, and run autoplaying content only while it is active.

groups.title: Tooling
groups.intro: Inspect and tear down the motions of a page, validate a definition as JSON, and test what an element shows.

groups.title: React
groups.intro: From @udixio/ui-react: a component that renders the animated element, a Presence that keeps leaving children, and hooks.

groups.title: Angular
groups.intro: From @udixio/ui-angular: standalone directives; add each to the imports of the component that uses it.

groups.title: Svelte
groups.intro: From @udixio/ui-svelte: attachments ({@attach …}) and a presence transition; options are passed as a function so they stay reactive.

html.title: HTML and CSS
html.intro: What connectMotion() reads in the markup, and what the runtime writes back. Each has a JavaScript equivalent.

items.name: data-motion
items.description: Binds the named motions: at most one per kind (a presence, an emphasis, a layout, a reveal or scrub, a loop). A second name of a kind the element already has is ignored. A name of a sequence binds that sequence.

items.name: hidden
items.on: an element with a presence motion
items.description: Setting it plays the exit: the element stays displayed and inert until the exit ends. Removing it plays the entry. An element inserted with it plays no entry.

items.name: data-motion-state
items.description: Each change of its value replays the emphasis.

items.name: data-motion-restore-focus
items.on: an element with a presence motion
items.description: Where focus goes when an exit starts with focus inside the element (WCAG 2.4.3). The selector is looked up in the document when the exit starts; an invalid selector or a match inside the element gives no target.

items.name: data-motion-paused
items.description: Pauses the loop while the attribute is present; removing it resumes the loop.

items.name: data-motion-shared
items.on: an element with a layout motion
items.description: The shared identity: the element morphs from the place of another element that held the same key.

items.name: data-motion-scope
items.description: The scope a layout motion watches: the closest ancestor with this attribute, or else the element’s parent. A move caused outside the scope is not animated.

items.name: data-motion-value
items.description: Binds the named values: each one is written on the element as --udx-motion-value-<name>; a value with a format writes its number as the element’s text.

items.name: data-motion-gesture
items.description: Binds the named gesture (a drag, a swipe or a reorder), with its keyboard alternative.

items.name: data-motion-step
items.on: a descendant of a sequence root
items.description: Marks the elements of a step of the sequence bound on the root; the elements of one step play together.

items.name: data-motion-policy
items.description: reduce applies the reduced-motion policy whatever the system says; auto, an absent attribute or an unknown value follow prefers-reduced-motion.

items.name: data-motion-presence
items.on: an element with a presence motion
items.description: Written by the runtime while the element enters, rests and leaves; authors do not set it. Style it with data-[motion-presence=exiting]:… variants.

items.name: data-motion-direction
items.description: Written by navigate() and connectAstroTransitions() for the length of a page transition.

items.name: --udx-motion-value-<name>
items.value: a number; with a unit, a second variable named after it (-deg, -px, -rem, -percent)
items.description: Written by a value binding for as long as the element is bound; read it in var() from any CSS property.

items.name: --udx-motion
items.description: none applies the end state without animating. A name plays that motion in place of the element’s own, when it is a defined motion of the same kind.

items.name: --udx-motion-scale
items.description: Scales the durations and the distances of the keyframes; 0 stops the motion. motion.css registers it and sets it to 0 under the reduced-motion policy.

items.name: --udx-motion-duration-*, --udx-motion-easing-*, --udx-motion-spring-*
items.description: The duration, easing and spring tokens as custom properties, for a CSS transition that follows the same timings: calc(var(--udx-motion-duration-medium2) * var(--udx-motion-scale)).

items.name: motion-[name], motion-none
items.description: Tailwind utilities from @udixio/tailwind that set --udx-motion, with any variant: md:motion-[fade] fades from md up, hover:motion-none turns it off on hover.

angular-Motion.name: Motion

inputs.name: udxMotion
inputs.description: The motion: the name of a defined motion, a definition, or a raw spec. A list of them, or names separated by spaces, binds one of each kind, the first listed.

inputs.name: udxMotionPresent
inputs.description:
Whether the element is present. The element stays in the DOM: `false` plays its exit, the element staying displayed
until the exit has finished, then `hidden` hides it; `true` removes `hidden` and plays its entry. An element absent
from its first render is `hidden` at once, in the server HTML too, so its content stays indexable. While it stays
`true`, the element's own `hidden` is left to the author.

inputs.name: udxMotionState
inputs.description: A value whose change replays an emphasis or a reveal.

inputs.name: udxMotionSettled
inputs.description: Skips the entry of an element that is already present, such as after server rendering.

inputs.name: udxMotionShared
inputs.description: The shared identity: a layout motion morphs from the place of another element that held the same key. A change binds the element again.

inputs.name: udxMotionPaused
inputs.description: Holds a loop while true and plays it again when false: a loop pauses by itself out of view, and this holds it for the author too (WCAG 2.2.2). Ignored without a loop.

inputs.name: udxMotionRestoreFocus
inputs.description: Where focus goes when an exit starts with focus inside the element: an element, or a function that gives one then. Read when the element binds.

methods.name: binding
methods.description: The core binding (handle: pause, reverse, seek), once bound: the presence if any, else the first.

methods.name: bindingOf
methods.description: The core binding of a kind, once bound.

methods.name: play
methods.description:
Replays an emphasis or a reveal, as the core binding's `play()` does. A replay asked before the motion is defined plays once
it is; a presence, a layout or a loop is left alone.

angular-Motion.description: Plays a named motion on the element it sits on, from `@udixio/motion`.

tags.devx:
- Put it on what enters and leaves: `@if (open()) {
…
}`. Angular keeps the element until the exit has played, then removes it. - For a node the template keeps in the DOM, bind `[udxMotionPresent]`: the exit plays when it turns `false`, then `hidden` hides the node, and the entry plays when it turns `true`, as for an HTML element with `hidden` and `data-motion`. Navigation and content (menus, tab panels, accordions) take it, so that their links and text are in the server HTML; transient UI (toasts, dialogs, list items) goes in an `@if`. - For an emphasis or a reveal, bind `[udxMotionState]` to the value that changes: `
tags.a11y:
- An exit keeps the element in the accessibility tree until it has played,
  and the core makes it `inert` meanwhile.
- With focus inside, an exit moves it to `[udxMotionRestoreFocus]` first, so
  the focus is not lost (WCAG 2.4.3); without that target the element stays
  focusable until focus leaves it.
tags.limitations:
- Content rendered by the server is marked present, so it does not replay its
  entry on hydration; `udxMotionSettled` still skips the entry of other content.
- A leave inside a child component's template follows Angular's own rule:
  apply the directive on the child host in the parent template.

angular-MotionGesture.name: MotionGesture

inputs.name: udxMotionGesture
inputs.description: The gesture: the name of a defined gesture, or its definition. A change binds the element again.

outputs.name: udxDragEnd
outputs.description: Emits the release of a drag, once it has come to rest; its `detail` is the offset `{ x, y }` it came to rest at.

outputs.name: udxSwipe
outputs.description: Emits each swipe, before it flies out. Preventing it keeps the element in place.

outputs.name: udxReorder
outputs.description: Emits each reorder step, before the element moves. Preventing it keeps the order.

methods.name: reset
methods.description: Puts the element back at offset 0, with the release spring. Does nothing before the element is bound.

angular-MotionGesture.description:
Gives the element it sits on a gesture of `@udixio/motion`: a drag that follows the pointer, a swipe that flies away, or a
reorder among its siblings, with its keyboard alternative. Each event of the gesture is emitted on its output, as the
`CustomEvent` the gesture dispatched: a handler that calls `$event.preventDefault()` keeps the element in place (a
swipe) or the order as it is (a reorder).

tags.devx:
- Bind it as `<li udxMotionGesture="swipe-dismiss" (udxSwipe)="remove(item)">`: a swiped row removes itself from the list.
- A reorder list prevents the move and moves the item in its state, so the template renders the new order and the layout
  motion animates it: `<li udxMotionGesture="reorder-row" (udxReorder)="onReorder($event)">`, with
  `onReorder(event: CustomEvent<{ from: number; to: number }>) { event.preventDefault(); this.move(event.detail); }`.
- Call `reset()` on the template reference `#row="udxMotionGesture"` to put the element back at offset 0.
tags.limitations: - The directive binds after the host has rendered, in the browser only: nothing is bound during server rendering.

angular-MotionSequence.name: MotionSequence

inputs.name: udxMotionSequence
inputs.description: The sequence: the name of a defined sequence, or its definition. A change binds the element again.

inputs.name: udxMotionSequenceSettled
inputs.description: Skips the entry: the content is already in its place, such as after server rendering.

methods.name: handle
methods.description: The handle of the latest play, or null before the first one.

methods.name: play
methods.description: Replays the sequence from its start. Does nothing until the sequence is bound.

angular-MotionSequence.description:
Plays a named sequence of `@udixio/motion` on the element it sits on: its children that carry `data-motion-step` are
its steps, and one handle plays the whole choreography.

tags.devx:
- Bind it as `<section udxMotionSequence="hero">`; read `handle` or call `play()` on the template reference
  `#hero="udxMotionSequence"` to replay it.
- A change of the name binds the new sequence settled, as `udxMotion` does: call `play()` to replay it.
tags.limitations:
- Server-rendered content replays its entry once the directive binds in the browser, unless
  `udxMotionSequenceSettled` is set.

angular-MotionValue.name: MotionValue

inputs.name: udxMotionValue
inputs.description: The value: the name of a defined value, or its definition. A change binds the element again.

outputs.name: udxMotionValueChange
outputs.description: Emits the number when the value comes to rest, and each change of its target: not on each frame.

methods.name: get
methods.description: The number the value holds, or undefined before the element is bound. Reading it never re-renders.

methods.name: set
methods.description: Moves a state value to a number, clamped to its range. Does nothing before the element is bound.

methods.name: subscribe
methods.description:
Calls the listener with each new number, on each frame, and returns its unsubscribe. A listener follows the element
when it is bound again.

angular-MotionValue.description:
Writes a named value of `@udixio/motion` on the element it sits on, as `--udx-motion-value-<name>`.

Reading the number with `get()` never re-renders anything. `udxMotionValueChange` emits when the value comes to rest and
when its target changes, not on each frame: to follow each frame, read the CSS variable `--udx-motion-value-<name>`, or
call `subscribe()`.

tags.devx:
- Bind it as `<div udxMotionValue="tilt">`: the card's class reads `--udx-motion-value-tilt`.
- A change of the name binds the element again: the old binding is destroyed.
- Read the number in a template handler, or call `get()` and `set(n)` on the template reference
  `#tilt="udxMotionValue"`.
tags.limitations:
- The directive binds after the host has rendered, in the browser only: nothing is written during server rendering.
- `udxMotionValueChange` does not emit on each frame: a pointer or scroll value emits at each change of its target, which
  follows the input events.

members.name: threshold
members.description:
The fraction of the element's area that must be in the view, from 0 (any part of it, the default) to 1 (all of it).
An element taller or wider than the view reaches at most the fraction of it that the view can hold.

api-ActiveState.name: ActiveState

members.name: inView
members.description: The element is in the view, past the threshold.

members.name: pageVisible
members.description: The document's tab is shown (`document.visibilityState` is not `hidden`).

members.name: reduced
members.description: Motion is reduced, by the system setting or by `<html data-motion-policy="reduce">`.

api-ActiveState.description: The three conditions of `watchActive`; the element is active when all of them hold.

api-amplitudeOf.name: amplitudeOf
api-amplitudeOf.description:
The keyframe at `amplitude` of its distance: `x`, `y` and `rotate` are multiplied by it, and a scale keeps its distance
from 1 (a scale of 2 at an amplitude of 0.5 is 1.5). The other fields are not distances and are kept: an opacity, a
drawn shape, a position along a path.

api-animateStyle.name: animateStyle
signatures: animateStyle(element: MotionElement, keyframes: StyleKeyframe | StyleKeyframe[], options?: AnimateStyleOptions): MotionHandle

params.name: element
params.description: The element whose style is animated.

params.name: keyframes
params.description: One keyframe (the end, from the current values) or several, in CSS property names.

params.name: options
params.description: The timing, the delay, the iterations, and whether to start from the current values.

api-animateStyle.description: Animates CSS properties of an element over a motion token, and leaves the element at its last frame.

api-AnimateStyleOptions.name: AnimateStyleOptions

members.name: timing
members.description:
The motion of the keyframes; `spring.default.spatial` by default. `--udx-motion-scale` multiplies its duration, and
a scale of 0 shows the end frame at once.

members.name: delay
members.description: Milliseconds before the motion starts; 0 by default.

members.name: iterations
members.description: How many times the motion plays, `Infinity` for a loop; 1 by default.

members.name: carry
members.description: Start from the element's current computed values; true by default for a single keyframe.

members.name: reduced
members.description: What reduced motion, `--udx-motion: none` or a motion scale of 0 shows: the last keyframe (the first one for a loop), the first, or a given frame.

api-AnimateStyleOptions.description: The options of `animateStyle`: its timing, its delay and repeats, whether it starts from the element, and its reduced frame.

api-applyFrame.name: applyFrame
api-applyFrame.description:
Write the visual fields of a frame inline. Never writes `transform`. A fully drawn shape keeps no dash inline. A
frame that is the state at rest goes through `applyRestingFrame`, which releases its neutral fields.

api-applyRestingFrame.name: applyRestingFrame
signatures: applyRestingFrame(target: MotionElement, frame: VisualFrame, owner?: DrawOwner): void
api-applyRestingFrame.description: Write a frame that is a state at rest (not a motion in progress), for `owner`: its neutral fields go back to the stylesheet.

api-applySplitFrame.name: applySplitFrame
signatures: applySplitFrame(target: MotionElement, spec: Splitting, runtime: MotionRuntime, frame: VisualFrame, resting?: boolean): void
api-applySplitFrame.description:
Write a frame on each piece of the text of an element, or on the element itself when its text does not split. A resting
frame releases its neutral fields on each of them (`applyRestingFrame`).

api-AxisProgress.name: AxisProgress
api-AxisProgress.description: A progress per axis: x drives the centre x and the width of a box, y its centre y and its height.

members.name: present
members.description: Whether the element starts present: false binds it absent, so that `setPresent(true)` plays its entry.

members.name: settled
members.description: Treat a present element as already in place: no entry plays when it is bound.

members.name: development
members.description: Report mistakes on the console: an unknown name, an invalid spec, an exit that holds focus with no `restoreFocus`.

members.name: shared
members.description: The shared identity of a layout motion: the element morphs from the place of another element that held the same key.

members.name: paused
members.description: A loop bound with `paused` starts paused (also when it is bound later, once its name is defined).

members.name: restoreFocus
members.description:
Where focus goes when an exit starts with focus inside the element: an element, or a function that gives one when the exit
starts. Without one outside the element, the element stays focusable until focus leaves it.

api-blink.name: blink
api-blink.description: Looping: one dim flash per second, under the three flashes a second of WCAG 2.3.1; the user can pause it.

api-Box.name: Box
api-Box.description: A box: centre and size, relative to its reference.

api-breathe.name: breathe
api-breathe.description: Looping: swells to 104% and back in one second; the user can pause it (WCAG 2.2.2).

api-cascade.name: cascade
api-cascade.description: A list entering together: each item fades in while rising 24px, one step after the previous one.

api-compareSamples.name: compareSamples
signatures: compareSamples(a: VisualState[], b: VisualState[], tol?: typeof TOLERANCES): { ok: boolean; failures: string[] }

api-composeHandles.name: composeHandles
api-composeHandles.description:
One handle that drives all the given handles together, on their common timeline: `delay` is the earliest child
delay, `duration` runs from there to the latest end of the children, and `seek` takes the delay-inclusive time of
the children, as `currentTime` does. Each child is clamped to its own end, delay included, so that a handle's end
is `delay + duration`, for a leaf and for a composition alike.

api-connectAstroTransitions.name: connectAstroTransitions
api-connectAstroTransitions.description:
Give Astro's ClientRouter transitions the motion direction and styles. Astro starts the View Transition itself, so this
adapter starts none: it sets the direction the motion CSS reads, on the page and on the document that Astro swaps in.
Under reduced motion or `--udx-motion: none` it does nothing. Returns a function that disconnects.

api-connectMotion.name: connectMotion

params.name: options
params.description: The root to scan, and the development reports.

returns.description: A function that disconnects the scanner and destroys its bindings.

api-connectMotion.description:
Bind the `[data-motion]` elements under `root` and keep the bindings in step with the DOM:
an insertion plays its entry, a removal destroys, and `data-motion`, `data-motion-state` and `hidden`
drive the motion. While `data-motion-paused` is set, the loop of the element is paused. An element may
list several motions, one per kind: of the names of a kind, the first listed is bound, and the others are ignored (and
reported in development). A `data-motion-shared` gives the layout motion of the element a shared
identity: it morphs from the place of another element with the same key. A `data-motion-value` binds the named values
of the element, each written as a variable there. A `data-motion` name that is a defined sequence binds the sequence
on the element; its `data-motion-step` children need no scanning of their own. A `data-motion-gesture` binds the gesture
it names on the element. A `data-motion-restore-focus="<selector>"` names the element focus moves to when an exit starts with
focus inside it. The values, the sequences and the gestures are loaded the first time a page meets one of them.
The returned function disconnects the scanner and destroys its bindings.

members.name: root
members.description: The subtree whose `data-motion`, `data-motion-value` and `data-motion-gesture` elements are bound and followed.

members.name: development
members.description: Report an unknown name or an invalid attribute on the console; the element is bound once the name is defined.

api-ContentPlan.name: ContentPlan

members.name: radii
members.description: The px corner radii of a box at rest, when it has any: they are kept round while the box is stretched.

api-ContentPlan.description:
A node of the content of a resizing element: its box before and after the move, what its stylesheet gives it,
and `unit`, the screen pixels per local pixel of its parent at rest (its translate is in local pixels).

api-ContinuousApi.name: ContinuousApi
api-ContinuousApi.description: The functions that bind a scrub and a loop, as the continuous module provides them once it has evaluated in this copy of the package.

api-continuousModule.name: continuousModule
api-continuousModule.description: The functions that bind a scrub and a loop, once the continuous module has evaluated in this copy of the package.

api-correctedRadius.name: correctedRadius
api-correctedRadius.description: The `border-radius` value that looks like `radii` on an element stretched by `k`: each radius is divided by the stretch of its axis.

api-createMotionPolicy.name: createMotionPolicy
api-createMotionPolicy.description: Make a new policy store, of the shape of `motionPolicy`: a page needs only the one `motionPolicy`.

api-createSpring.name: createSpring

params.name: initial
params.description: The number to start at.

params.name: options
params.description: The spring, and the callbacks that receive each value and the rest.

api-createSpring.description: A number that follows its target over a spring, for values that drive layout or script.

api-cssProvider.name: cssProvider
api-cssProvider.description:
Experimental CSS keyframe provider. Requires a connected light-DOM target controlled by
the consumer, without author animations or !important rules masking animated properties.
Only two complete frames with matching opacity/x/y/scale/rotate fields are supported.
Easing accepts standard keywords, steps() and cubic-bezier() without nested
functions (including calc()), plus exact generated token linear.easing strings.
Other linear() values, substitutions and CSS-wide values are unsupported. Duration and
delay remain explicit; callers must select the complete fallback pair when unsupported.
Cascade changes and writes between synchronous checks cannot be reliably detected.

api-cssTiming.name: cssTiming
signatures: cssTiming(timing: SpringRef | CurveTiming): { duration: string; easing: string }

params.name: timing
params.description: A spring token or a curve.

returns.description: A CSS `duration` and `easing`, for a transition or an animation.

api-cssTiming.description:
The CSS `transition-duration` and `transition-timing-function` of a motion token, for a stylesheet. A spring names the
`--udx-motion-spring-*` custom properties of `motion.css`, with the official cubic-bezier fallback of the expressive
scheme when the stylesheet is absent; a curve is its duration in milliseconds and its CSS easing. Pure: it reads no
document, so it is safe on the server.

api-CurveTiming.name: CurveTiming

members.name: duration
members.description: How long the motion lasts.

members.name: easing
members.description: How its progress accelerates and slows down.

api-CurveTiming.description: A timing as a curve: a duration token and an easing token, in place of a spring.

api-deferredHandle.name: deferredHandle
signatures: deferredHandle(): { handle: MotionHandle; readonly cancelled: boolean; resolve(real: MotionHandle): void }

returns.type: { handle: MotionHandle; readonly cancelled: boolean; resolve(real: MotionHandle): void }

api-deferredHandle.description:
A handle that exists before its animation: commands wait for the real handle, except cancel.
`cancelled` tells whether the handle was cancelled before its real handle arrived.

api-DeferredMotion.name: DeferredMotion

members.name: binding
members.description: The binding, once the motion is defined.

members.name: setPresent
members.description:
Set the presence of the element: `setPresent` of the binding when it is a presence motion, else nothing. Asked before the
name is defined, the last value is kept and applied when the motion is defined; resolves at once in that case.

members.name: play
members.description:
Replay an emphasis or a reveal, as the binding's `play()` does; asked before the name is defined, the replay happens once
the motion is defined. A presence, a layout, a loop or a scrub is left alone.

members.name: destroy
members.description: Destroy the binding, or stop waiting for the name to be defined.

api-DeferredMotion.description: A motion that is bound, or waits for its name to be defined.

api-definedMotions.name: definedMotions
api-definedMotions.description: The names of the defined motions, in definition order.

params.name: spec

api-defineMotion.description:
Define a named motion. Re-defining a name with an identical spec returns the
existing reference; a different spec throws. The spec is validated in development only:
a production build trusts the definition.

params.name: name
params.description: A kebab-case name, unique on the page.

params.name: spec

api-defineSequence.description:
Define a named sequence. Re-defining a name with an identical spec returns the existing reference; a different spec
throws. The spec is validated in development only.

Name a shared identity: the layout motions that bear the same name follow one element into another (a thumbnail
that becomes the card it opens). Validated like a motion name, and returned as given.

api-defineTokens.name: defineTokens
api-defineTokens.description: Select a product-wide M3 scheme. Durations are in milliseconds.

params.description: A kebab-case name; it names the variable `--udx-motion-value-<name>`.

params.name: spec

Define a named value. Re-defining a name with an identical spec returns the existing reference; a different spec
throws. The name is kebab-case, checked always; the spec is validated in development only.

api-distanceScaleOf.name: distanceScaleOf
api-distanceScaleOf.description:
The amplitude of the distances a motion plays on `target`: its motion scale, or 1 where no distance moves, which is under
reduced motion (`reduced`) and under `--udx-motion: none`.

api-draw.name: draw
api-draw.description: Entering a path or a basic shape: its stroke is drawn from nothing to the whole shape.

api-DurationToken.name: DurationToken

api-easingOf.name: easingOf

api-gesture.description:
Bind a gesture to an element. It moves the element with the pointer and gives it a keyboard alternative. While it is
bound, the element's touch-action leaves to the browser only the pan the gesture does not use. The arrows of a drag
move it physically, and in right-to-left text the arrows of a reorder on x follow the reading direction. The element
carries one gesture at a time: binding another one destroys the previous one. The gesture writes the element's `translate` (and
`opacity` while a swipe flies out), so an author's own `translate` on that element is overwritten while it is bound.
The `development` option only reports a reorder bound on an element with no parent.

A gesture on an element. `drag` follows the pointer on `axis`, within its parent when `bounds` is `parent`. `swipe`
follows it on one axis, and flies it out when it is released far or fast enough. `reorder` moves it among the siblings
that carry the same gesture, on one axis. `release` is the spring of the release. `alternative` names the keyboard
alternative of the kind: arrows move a drag, a key swipes, and Space, arrows and Escape reorder; it is inferred from the
kind when the spec leaves it out. `afterFlyOut` is taken by a swipe only: `hide` (the default) keeps the element in the
DOM, out of assistive technology's sight, and `remove` takes it out of the DOM once it has flown out.

api-motion.description:
Bind a motion to an element. The binding owns its presence (`data-motion-presence`, `inert`),
its replays and its cleanup. An element carries one motion of each kind: a call with a motion of a
kind the element already holds replaces it, destroying the old binding (which is then inert); the
bindings of the other kinds are kept. A list of names is not a series of calls: `motionsWhenDefined`
and `connectMotion` keep the first listed name of each kind.

members.description: The verb of the bound definition.

members.name: kind
members.description: The kind of the binding: `presence`, `emphasis`, `layout`, `view` (a reveal or a scrub) or `loop`.

members.description: Whether a loop is paused at the author's request; undefined for the other kinds.

members.name: play
members.description:
Replay an emphasis or a reveal from its first frame, resume a loop, or compare a layout and move it now. Throws for
`appear` and `disappear`, which take `setPresent`.

members.name: pause
members.description: Pause a loop, at the author's request (WCAG 2.2.2); `play()` resumes it. Refused for every other kind.

members.name: setPresent
members.description:
Run the exit (`false`) or the entry (`true`) of a presence motion. Resolves to `'finished'` or `'cancelled'` and never
rejects: on a failure the element is left in its destination state.

members.name: destroy
members.description:
Cancel the motion and release the inline state it wrote. The binding is then inert: `setPresent` resolves `'finished'` at
once, `play` returns a finished handle and `pause` does nothing, without touching the element (a call that does not apply
to its kind still throws).

api-ValueSpec.description:
A continuous number an element can use in CSS: written as `--udx-motion-value-<name>` on each bound element.
`axis` is taken by `pointer` (`x`, `y`, or `both`, which writes two channels, `-x` and `-y`) and `scroll` (`block` or
`inline`). `spring` smooths the value and keeps its velocity when the target moves again; `none` writes it at once.
`unit` also writes the number with the unit, in a second variable named after the unit (`-deg`, `-px`, `-rem`, `-percent`).
`timing` is taken by `time` only, for its period:
its `duration` is the period, and its `easing` is not applied to the progress.
`format` is taken by `state` only: the number is also written as text, in the page's language, and it counts up when
the element scrolls into view. `currency` is an ISO 4217 code, required with the `currency` format and refused otherwise.

A scroll container ends the search: the visitor scrolls its content into view, so the element's own box decides.

react-Motion.name: Motion
react-Motion.description:
Renders an element that holds a motion of `@udixio/motion`: `name` is what `useMotion` takes, and the element is `as` (a
`div` by default) with the props it takes. The motion binds to that element, and a `gesture` binds to the same element, so
one element can hold a presence, a layout and a gesture without merging refs. `present` plays the entry and the exit of
an element that stays in the DOM, `hidden` while absent; a `Presence` removes a child that leaves, once its exit has played.

tags.devx:
- For a replay, call `play()` from `useMotion`. A `ref` gives the element too, and `getMotion(element, 'emphasis')?.play()`
  (or `'view'` for a reveal) from `@udixio/motion` replays it from there.
- Inside a `Presence`, the presence is the child's: a child that is removed plays its exit before it leaves.
- Transient UI (toasts, dialogs, list items) is rendered conditionally, in a `Presence`; navigation and content take
  `present`, so that they stay in the DOM.
- Without `present`, the element's own `hidden` prop is left to the author.
tags.limitations:
- `name` is the motion of the element, so the element's own `name` attribute cannot be set with this component: a `ref` sets
  it.
- The element must take a `ref` that is a DOM element, as with `useMotion`.

// A submenu that stays in the DOM, hidden while closed: its links are in the server HTML.

react-Presence.name: Presence
react-Presence.description:
Keeps the children that leave it rendered until their exit has played, so that a removed `Motion` plays its exit before it
leaves the page. It renders no element of its own: the children are the elements of the parent.

A `Motion` inside a child is given the presence of the child: a child in the children is present and enters, and a child
that left is kept and exits. Once every motion of a child has finished its exit, the child is removed. A child that holds no
motion leaves at once. A child added in a render enters in that render, with the others added with it.

tags.devx:
- Give each child a `key`: it is how the Presence knows which child left. A child without one is kept by its position, and
  development reports it.
- A child that left keeps the props it had when it left, so its content plays its exit as it was.
- A child keeps its place while it leaves: after the child before it that is still rendered, or first when there is none.
- Children of a Presence are removed in the order their exits end. A child that comes back before its exit has played is
  kept, and its exit is cancelled.
tags.limitations:
- The exits exist in the browser only: a server render shows the current children.
- Only a `Motion` reports its exit to the Presence. A child whose motion is run by a `useMotion` hook instead leaves at once,
  without its exit.

examples:
// A single conditional child: it enters when it appears, and leaves once its exit has played.
<Presence>{open && <Motion key="panel" name="slide">…</Motion>}</Presence>

react-useMotion.name: useMotion
signatures: useMotion<T extends MotionElement = HTMLElement>(source: MotionSource | readonly MotionSource[], options?: UseMotionOptions): UseMotionReturn<T>
react-useMotion.description:
Connects a React element to one or more named motions of `@udixio/motion`.

The hook holds no animation logic: it binds the element through the core
(`motionsWhenDefined`), tells the binding when `present` changes, keeps the
element rendered until its exit has finished, and replays an emphasis or a
reveal when `state` changes. Several sources, a list or names separated by spaces, bind
each of them to the element, one per kind, so one element can hold a presence and a layout.
Render the element while `mounted` is true and put `ref` on it.

tags.devx:
- `mounted` stays true while an exit plays, so the element is removed only
  once the exit has finished. Do not unmount it yourself on `present`.
- An element rendered with `hidden={!present}` stays in the DOM, as in HTML:
  when `present` turns false it stays displayed while its exit plays, then
  `hidden` hides it and its neighbours make room; when it turns true, the
  entry plays. Use it for navigation and content, whose links and text must
  be in the server HTML; render transient UI with `mounted`.
- An emphasis or a reveal replays on each change of `state`. Only `appear`
  and `disappear` have a presence: when `present` turns false, any other
  motion is removed at once, without an exit.
- Hydrated server content is treated as already in place, so the first
  attach plays no entry; a later remount plays it.
- An element carries one motion of each kind: of two sources of one kind,
  such as `['fade', 'slide']`, the first listed is bound and the other is
  ignored, reported in development. Define one motion whose keyframes do both.
tags.limitations:
- The element must accept a `ref` that is a DOM element. A component that
  does not forward its ref cannot be animated.
- The motion is bound to the element itself, not to its children.

examples:
// A list item that enters and leaves, and moves when its neighbours change.
const item = useMotion(['fade', 'reflow'], { present });

// A thumbnail and its detail share a key: the detail morphs out of the thumbnail.
const detail = useMotion('reflow', { shared: `pic-${id}` });

// A spinner that turns while loading and holds still otherwise: a loop pauses by itself out of view.
const spinner = useMotion('rotate', { paused: !loading });
